comment: Cross-renderer parity fixtures. See qa/cross-renderer-parity-design.md for the design. Each fixture references an item.json under renderer/tests/fixtures/<uuid>/ + a checked-in Rust golden under renderer/tests/golden/<golden>.png. The harness captures the browser side fresh via Playwright + diffs against the golden (which render_tests.sh's GREEN gate keeps in sync with the Rust path). Thresholds start lax; tighten as drift is fixed. Note: image_slide fixture (planned in design doc) deferred to commit 3 -- parity-harness.html's drawCanvas path only renders text_slide shape; image-asset rendering needs a separate browser-side hydrator. Commit-2 first wave is 5 fixtures, not 6.

fixtures.name: parity_text_static
fixtures.purpose: Text-only static slide. Canvas2D vs fontdue text AA + word-wrap parity.

fixtures.name: parity_text_emoji_basic
fixtures.purpose: SDF arc slice C.3 -- mixed MSDF + color-emoji text. 'Hi! 🌟' exercises the layout-side codepoint segmentation (U+1F31F is in the baked U+1F000-1FFFF range) and the per-page emoji draw batch. Canvas2D side renders via ui/styles.css's @font-face for Noto Color Emoji using the same unicode-range; Rust side renders via FS_EMOJI sampling the build-time-baked CBDT atlas.

fixtures.name: parity_motion_ticker
fixtures.purpose: Ticker motion @ tick=1.75. Motion-phase math + per-tick frequency tables.
fixtures.divergent_reason: ticker structural divergence: Rust offset_x_norm = 1 - 2*cycle (single-copy NDC offset, text enters from right at cycle=0) vs Canvas2D / Python np.roll wrap-around two-copy (text at original position at phase=0, wraps via box-width copy). Both correct for their context (device vs editor preview); not pixel-comparable.

fixtures.name: parity_motion_compound
fixtures.purpose: 4-layer compound motion (blink+shake+pulse+bounce) at tick 0.5. Different motion mix than parity_motion_ticker; surfaces multi-motion-phase drift.
fixtures.divergent_reason: compound motion includes shake (different RNG families: FNV-1a string hash on Canvas2D vs splitmix64 u64 hash on Rust -- structurally different random sequences per layer) and bounce (Rust abs(sin) ball-on-floor per qarl 2026-05-03 device decision vs Canvas2D plain sin symmetric). Both correct for their context.

fixtures.name: parity_transition_fade
fixtures.divergent_reason: transition's TO slide (2c858968) has 5 ticker-motion text layers; ticker structural divergence (Rust right-edge-start single-copy vs Canvas2D wrap two-copy) flows through into every transition compositor's input. Independent of the transition shader/JS math itself. Same root cause as parity_motion_ticker; divergence flows through the transition compositor regardless of which transition shader handles the AB blend.
fixtures.purpose: Cross-fade midpoint. JS per-pixel (1-t)·A + t·B vs Rust FS_FADE.

fixtures.name: parity_animated_uncage
fixtures.purpose: Motion (shake) + background_pattern (gradient) at the same tick. Closes the UNCAGE-gradient-missing regression class — surface where inline-preview previously dropped pattern bg silently.
fixtures.divergent_reason: shake structural divergence: Canvas2D uses FNV-1a string-hash gaussian, Rust uses splitmix64 u64-hash gaussian. Different RNG families = different per-layer random offset sequences (same structural shape as confetti's by-design RNG-family divergence).

fixtures.name: parity_animated_stripes_bounce
fixtures.purpose: Motion (bounce) + background_pattern (stripes). Different motion-pattern pair than halftone/pulse so a drift hits two fixtures, not one.
